Moving Towards a New Learning Agenda: AKU Teaching Champions

content.text: The Network of Teaching and Learning launched its first bi-monthly learning session for AKU's Teaching Champions on March 12, 2015. These learning sessions are intended to develop a community of practice and enquiry, thereby contributing to the scholarship of teaching and learning at AKU.

The learning session, which was titled "Engaged Learning: Are We All on the Same Page?" was attended by 29 faculty members from across AKU's schools and institutes: SONAM, East Africa and Pakistan; IED, East Africa; DED; and Medical College.

Effective teaching and engaged learning are often used in the same breath and, therefore, the session set out to explore the following questions: What exactly is engaged learning? Why is it important? What are its manifestations in our classrooms? How do we ensure that it occurs in our classrooms? What is the student's role in this process? What is AKU's vision of and strategy for engaged learning? The session was abuzz with discussion throughout.

At the end of the session, one participant, Raheel Lakhani, Educational Technologist, commented: "I really enjoyed your session... I really like the model you shared and it makes so much sense for both curriculum design and pedagogy, and fostering autonomy and lifelong learning which service industry demands. Your session was very engaging."
The AKU Teaching and Learning Framework provides a shared understanding of teaching excellence.
For more information, contact Jane Rarieya, Assistant Director, TL_net.
